definition: Done routinely with little care or interest.
example: She offered a perfunctory greeting and returned to work.
nuance: Perfunctory suggests going through the motions, not simply being efficient.
prompt: A supervisor signs off on a report.
options: His perfunctory review consisted of a quick glance before signing.
His perfunctory review involved weeks of meticulous scrutiny.
He gave the report a perfunctory review with intense curiosity and care.
The review was perfunctory because it reached the right conclusion.
reasons: A token glance shows little investment in the task.
Correctness alone does not indicate care or its absence.

practice.prompt: A museum tour guide is leading her tenth group of the day.
options: By her last tour, her explanations had grown perfunctory, recited flatly while she glanced at the clock.
Her perfunctory tour ran three hours over because she answered every question in loving detail.
The museum's new elevator was perfunctory, so visitors using wheelchairs could reach every single floor.
In a perfunctory tone, she ordered the noisy guests to stop talking at once and permitted no reply.
reasons: Reciting in a flat voice while watching the clock shows she is only going through the motions.
Generous, enthusiastic attention is the reverse of routine, half-hearted effort.
This confuses the word with functional; it describes careless effort, not working equipment.
A commanding order that allows no reply is peremptory, a look-alike with a different meaning.
